correctness.rationale: The half-central-angle equation is continuous and strictly increasing on the relevant radius interval, so the polygon exists uniquely. Fresh integer recurrence reconstruction gives \(\deg P=384\) and \(\deg Q=768\); the constant coefficient has exact \(769\)-adic valuation two, degrees one through 383 have valuation at least two, degrees 384 through 767 at least one, and the leading coefficient valuation zero. These points lie on or above the segment from \((0,2)\) to \((768,0)\), with endpoints attained, so the Newton polygon has reduced slope \(-1/384\). Each local irreducible factor degree is divisible by 384, hence the geometric root has global degree 384 or 768, neither a power of two. The standard constructibility-degree criterion then proves nonconstructibility.

evidence: The prior theorem covers every odd \(n\ge8\) existentially, including \(n=771\).
Its proof uses limit and Hilbert-irreducibility machinery to obtain unspecified integer specializations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad existence theorem does not mechanically certify the specific side pair \(768,769\) with multiplicities \(769,2\).

originality.rationale: Czédli--Kunos Theorem 1.1(iv) already proves the broader existential fact that every odd order at least eight admits some nonconstructible cyclic polygon with at most two integer side lengths. It therefore covers existence at order 771, but does not imply nonconstructibility of this concrete multiset. Full-text inspection found no occurrence of 768, 769, or 771, and Resultary returned the assigned explicit witness as the exact hit. The originality claim is properly limited to the explicit consecutive-length witness and its local certificate.
residual_risks: An explicit identical witness could exist in unindexed notes, code, or literature despite the primary-paper and Resultary searches.
The general existence statement at order 771 is prior art; only the concrete witness and certificate are assessed as new.

final_claim: The convex cyclic \(771\)-gon with \(769\) sides of length \(768\) and two sides of length \(769\) exists and is not straightedge-and-compass constructible from its side lengths; the circumradius parameter satisfies a degree-\(768\) polynomial whose \(769\)-adic Newton polygon is the single slope \(-1/384\), forcing its minimal degree to be \(384\) or \(768\).
limitations: No minimality or uniqueness of the side lengths is claimed.
The 2015 general existential theorem remains strictly broader in orders covered.
